How do you care for an areca palm in the UAE?

Areca palm care in the UAE comes down to three things: bright indirect light away from harsh sun through glass, soil that stays moist but never soggy, and a pot with a drainage hole. Water when the top of the soil feels dry, not on a fixed schedule. The areca palm (Chrysalidocarpus lutescens) is non-toxic to cats and dogs (ASPCA).

Chrysalidocarpus lutescens (syn. Dypsis lutescens) · Also called Butterfly palm, Golden cane palm, Yellow palm, Golden feather palm, نخلة الأريكا
By the PlantsWorld team · Updated 12 November 2026

Areca Palm quick facts

LightBright indirect light indoors. Outdoors, partial shade; protect from summer midday sun.
WaterKeep moist, not soggy. Water thoroughly when the soil surface dries; never let it stand in water.
TemperatureIdeal 18–21 °C at night and 24–29 °C by day (Clemson). Chilling damage below 7 °C.
HumidityLikes high humidity. Below 50%, use a pebble tray or a humidifier (Clemson).
ACKeep it out of the direct cold airflow from a vent (Clemson: protect palms from draughts near air conditioning).
Outdoors in UAEYes, in shade or partial shade, with protection on cold inland winter nights.
PetsNon-toxic to cats and dogs (ASPCA). People should not eat the heart-of-palm.
Size indoorsAbout 1.8–2.1 m; grows about 15–25 cm a year (Clemson)
Main pestSpider mites
RepottingEvery 2 or 3 years, when the roots fill the pot (NC State, Clemson)

Is an areca palm right for you?

A good fit if

  • You have a cat or a dog and want a large plant that the ASPCA lists as non-toxic.
  • You have a bright room, such as a living room or an office near a large window.
  • You want a tall, feathery floor plant that fills a corner.
  • You are happy to check the soil regularly and water before it dries out completely.

Think twice if

  • Your room is dim, far from any window: areca palms need bright light.
  • You often forget to water: an areca palm does not like to dry out.
  • Your only space is a small shelf: areca palms grow tall and wide and need room.

How much light and sun does an areca palm need?

An areca palm needs bright, indirect light indoors. Clemson Extension recommends a spot near an east-, west- or south-facing window, and NC State Extension also says bright indirect light. Clemson also says that most palms need bright natural light all year.

In the UAE, strong sun through west- or south-facing glass can be too much for an areca palm in summer. Filtered light is the aim: a sheer curtain between the palm and the glass gives bright light without the harsh afternoon sun. Many towers have tinted glazing, which lowers indoor light, so a spot close to the window is often right.

Outdoors, NC State says the areca palm tolerates full sun but prefers partial shade, and UF/IFAS says small palms benefit from some shade until they are several feet tall. Young areca palms in full sun develop yellow leaves (UF/IFAS).

How often should you water an areca palm in Dubai?

Water an areca palm when the surface of the soil feels dry, and do not let the whole pot dry out. NC State Extension says to keep the soil moist but not soggy during the growing season, and Clemson Extension says palms should never dry out or stand in water. There is no fixed number of days: the soil tells you when.

To check whether an areca palm needs water, push a finger or a wooden skewer into the soil. If the top feels dry and the soil below is only slightly damp, water. If the soil is still wet near the surface, wait and check again later.

Many things change how fast an areca palm's pot dries. Small pots, terracotta, bright light and a warm spot dry quickly. Large plastic or glazed pots, a dim room and cool AC dry slowly. Humid coastal homes dry more slowly than inland homes, and outdoor pots dry fastest in summer heat and wind.

Water an areca palm thoroughly, until water runs out of the drainage hole. Then empty the saucer once the pot stops dripping (Clemson).

  • UAE tap water is desalinated and then remineralised, and its mineral content varies by area and building. If you see a white crust on the soil or pot, or brown leaf tips, flush the pot with plenty of water or switch to filtered water.
  • Pick up the pot just after watering and again when the soil feels dry. The difference in weight soon tells you when the palm needs water.

Does an areca palm need humidity under AC?

Yes, an areca palm prefers high humidity (NC State Extension). AC rooms in the UAE are not always dry: some homes are humid, others feel dry. A small hygrometer tells you which you have.

Clemson Extension says that if indoor humidity is below 50%, fill the pot saucer with gravel and water to raise the moisture level around the palm, or use a room humidifier. Keep the bottom of the pot above the water line so the roots do not sit in water.

Keep the areca palm out of the direct airflow from an AC vent. Clemson advises protecting palms from draughts near doors, windows and air conditioning. To test a spot, hold your hand where the fronds will be: if you feel a cold draught, move the palm.

What soil and pot does an areca palm need?

Grow an areca palm in a well-drained potting soil (NC State Extension). A good indoor potting mix with some perlite added drains well and still holds moisture. Heavy garden soil stays wet and can rot the roots.

Always grow an areca palm in a pot with a drainage hole. A decorative pot without a hole is fine as an outer cover, as long as you lift the inner pot out to drain after watering.

Shop: Universal Potting Soil – Holland, Perlite – Amorphous Volcanic Glass

How often should you fertilise an areca palm?

Fertilise an areca palm two to three times a year in spring and summer, with a slow-release palm fertiliser (Clemson Extension). Clemson recommends an analysis like 12-4-12 or 8-2-12. Too much fertiliser harms palms and can turn the tips of the lower leaves brown.

Palm fertilisers are high in potassium, which matters for an areca palm. UF/IFAS says older areca palm leaves often turn yellow from potassium deficiency, and potassium deficiency always shows first on the oldest leaves. Potassium deficiency is less common in pots than in sandy garden soil (UF/IFAS). When you correct it, UF/IFAS also advises adding magnesium, so a palm fertiliser that contains both is the simple choice.

When and how should you repot an areca palm?

Repot an areca palm only when the roots fill the pot. NC State Extension says every 2 or 3 years, and Clemson Extension says palms do best with confined roots and may need repotting only every two to three years. Signs are roots that grow out of the drainage hole or over the soil surface, or a palm that wilts between normal waterings (Illinois Extension).

Palm roots are fragile and easy to damage (Clemson), so handle the root ball gently and choose a pot only a little larger. In the UAE, repot in the cooler months from October to April, not in the peak of summer, and give a new plant time to settle before you repot it.

  1. Choose a pot only a little larger, with a drainage hole, and fresh well-drained potting mix.
  2. Gently knock the palm out of the old pot (Illinois Extension). Do not pull on the stems.
  3. Do not break up the root ball. Remove only loose old soil from the outside.
  4. Set the palm at the same depth as before, fill around it with new mix and press it gently.
  5. Water thoroughly and let the pot drain.

Shop: Universal Potting Soil – Holland

Should you cut yellow or brown fronds off an areca palm?

Cut off an areca palm frond only when it is completely brown and dead. UF/IFAS explains that old fronds are a source of potassium for new growth, and its research found that regular removal of discoloured potassium-deficient leaves speeds up the decline and can kill the palm.

You cannot prune an areca palm back to make it shorter. Clemson Extension explains that new growth comes from a high central growing point, so palms cannot be pruned back to reduce their height. If the palm is too tall, give it a larger space.

How do you propagate an areca palm?

An areca palm is propagated by division or by seed (NC State Extension, UF/IFAS). Division is the practical way at home, because an areca palm grows as a clump of many stems. Clemson Extension notes that most palms are grown from seed and only some can be divided.

Division is a big job for an areca palm, because the roots are fragile. Divide only a large, healthy, crowded clump, in the cooler months from October to April.

  1. Take the palm out of its pot and lay it on its side.
  2. Gently loosen the root ball and separate it into pieces by hand. Use a clean knife only if the roots are too tight to pull apart (Iowa State Extension).
  3. Make sure each piece has healthy fronds, stems and roots. Larger pieces recover more quickly (Iowa State Extension).
  4. Pot each piece straight away in fresh potting mix, at the same depth as before, so the roots do not dry out (Illinois Extension).
  5. Water thoroughly and keep the new pots in bright indirect light, out of direct sun, while they settle.

What should you do in the first week after your areca palm arrives?

A new areca palm needs time to settle into your home. In the first week, steady conditions matter more than extra care.

  1. Put the palm in bright indirect light, away from direct sun and out of the airflow from AC vents.
  2. Leave it in one spot. Moving it again and again slows the settling in.
  3. Check the soil with a finger before you water. Water only when the surface feels dry.
  4. Do not repot or feed it yet. Let it settle in its delivery pot first.
  5. Look under the fronds for fine webbing or tiny moving dots (spider mites), so you can act early.

How does areca palm care change through the UAE year?

Summer May–Sep

Indoors, check the soil often, keep it out of direct sun through glass, and keep it out of the direct AC airflow. Outdoor palms need shade from the midday and afternoon sun; summer nights stay hot, so outdoor pots dry very fast. Watch for spider mites.

Autumn Oct–Nov

Autumn is a good time to repot or divide an areca palm, and to move palms back to balconies and terraces. Move them outside gradually, starting in shade.

Winter Dec–Feb

Growth slows down, so the soil dries more slowly: check before you water and water less often. Coastal winter nights are mild. Inland (Al Ain, desert areas) and in Riyadh or Kuwait, nights can fall below 7 °C, when palms get chilling damage: move outdoor palms to a sheltered spot or indoors on cold nights. Make sure outdoor pots drain after rain.

Spring Mar–Apr

Start feeding again with a palm fertiliser. Spring is a good second window for repotting. Move outdoor palms into shade before May.

Why are the older leaves on my areca palm turning yellow?

Yellowing that starts on the oldest, lowest areca palm fronds can be potassium deficiency. UF/IFAS says older leaves on areca palms often turn yellow from a lack of potassium, and the leaves are often speckled with bronze or yellow. Potassium deficiency is less common in pots than in sandy garden soil. A healthy old frond dies quickly, from green to brown in a few days; old fronds that stay half-yellow for months usually lack potassium (UF/IFAS).

How to tell: Translucent yellow or orange spots on older leaflets, then brown, frizzled leaflet tips and edges. New fronds stay green.

How to fix it:

  1. Feed with a palm fertiliser that contains potassium and magnesium, at the rate on the label.
  2. Do not cut off the yellow fronds. Remove a frond only when it is completely brown and dead.
  3. Be patient: UF/IFAS says treatment may take one to two years or longer, because the palm may need to replace all its fronds.

Why is my areca palm turning yellow with wet soil?

Yellow areca palm fronds with soil that stays wet mean the roots are getting too much water. Root rot organisms thrive in wet, poorly drained potting mix (Iowa State Extension), and rotting roots cannot take up water, so the palm yellows and wilts.

How to tell: Soil still wet days after watering, water standing in the saucer or cover pot, lower fronds that wilt first.

How to fix it:

  1. Stop watering until the soil surface is dry.
  2. Empty the saucer or the decorative cover pot.
  3. If the soil stays wet, take the palm out and check the roots: healthy roots are firm and white; rotten roots are mushy and brown (Iowa State Extension).
  4. Repot into fresh, well-drained mix in a pot with a drainage hole if the old mix stays soggy.

Why are my areca palm leaf tips turning brown?

Brown leaf tips on an areca palm come from dry air, a lack of water or too much fertiliser (Clemson Extension). Salts from water and fertiliser that build up in the pot cause it too (Colorado State Extension).

How to tell: Crispy brown tips, sometimes with a white crust on the soil or the pot rim.

How to fix it:

  1. Check the humidity with a hygrometer. Below 50%, use a pebble tray or a humidifier.
  2. Do not let the pot dry out completely between waterings.
  3. Flush the pot with plenty of water to wash out salts, and use filtered water if the crust comes back.
  4. Feed only two to three times a year in spring and summer.

What is the fine webbing on my areca palm?

Fine webbing and pale, speckled fronds on an areca palm are spider mites. Clemson Extension says areca palms are very susceptible to spider mites, and that mites are often a problem indoors because of low humidity and warm temperatures.

How to tell: Tiny moving dots under the leaflets, fine webs between leaflets, a dusty, pale or bronze look on the fronds.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm away from other plants.
  2. Rinse the fronds, especially the undersides, with a strong shower of water.
  3. Spray the whole palm, especially the undersides of the leaflets, with a horticultural oil or neem oil spray, which can help control spider mites (Colorado State Extension). Repeat as the label says.
  4. Raise the humidity around the palm with a pebble tray or a humidifier.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

Why are my areca palm fronds sticky with black marks?

Sticky areca palm fronds with small brown or white bumps are a sign of scale insects, and the black film that follows is sooty mould growing on the sticky residue. UF/IFAS lists scale followed by sooty mould as a problem for areca palms; mealybugs also attack palms (Clemson).

How to tell: Small, still bumps on stems and leaflets, sticky leaves or floor below, a black sooty film, white cotton tufts (mealybugs).

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm away from other plants.
  2. Rub or pick the scale bumps off by hand (Colorado State Extension).
  3. Dab mealybugs with a cotton bud dipped in rubbing alcohol (Iowa State Extension). Test it on one leaflet first, because alcohol can burn leaves.
  4. Spray with a horticultural oil or neem oil spray and repeat as the label says. Colorado State Extension says spray oils are the most effective treatment for scales.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

Why is my areca palm pale or yellow in a sunny spot?

An areca palm that turns pale yellow or bleached in a sunny spot is getting too much direct sun. UF/IFAS says young areca palms in full sun develop yellow leaves, and that the yellowing can be reduced with shade.

How to tell: Pale fronds on the side that faces the window or the sun.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm out of direct sun, or add a sheer curtain on the window.
  2. Outdoors, give it shade from the midday and afternoon sun from May to September.

Why are my areca palm fronds drooping?

Drooping or wilting areca palm fronds mean the palm is short of water. Either the soil has dried out, or rotting roots can no longer take water up. Iowa State Extension warns that root rot is often mistaken for a lack of water, so check the soil before you water.

How to tell: Soil dry deep in the pot (thirst), or soil that is still wet (root damage).

How to fix it:

  1. If the soil is dry, water thoroughly until water runs out of the drainage hole.
  2. If the soil is wet, check the roots and follow the fix for yellow fronds with wet soil.

Why does my areca palm have brown patches after a cold night?

Reddish-brown dead areas that appear on the fronds a few days after a cold night are chilling damage (Clemson Extension). Clemson says most houseplant palms need temperatures above 7 °C (45 °F) to prevent chilling damage. In the UAE this happens outdoors inland, in the mountains and in colder GCC cities, and rarely on the coast.

How to tell: Damage on the most exposed fronds a few days after a cold night outdoors, or next to a cold door or window.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the palm to a sheltered spot or indoors on cold nights.
  2. Leave the damaged fronds until they are completely brown, then cut them off at the base.

What mistakes kill an areca palm?

MistakeDo this instead
Watering on a fixed weekly scheduleWater when the surface of the soil feels dry. Check with a finger or a skewer first.
Letting the pot dry out completelyKeep the soil moist but not soggy. Areca palms are less forgiving of drought than snake plants.
A pot with no drainage hole, or a saucer left full of waterUse a pot with a hole, or lift the inner pot out of a cover pot to drain. Empty the saucer after watering.
Summer afternoon sun through a west- or south-facing windowBright, filtered light, or a sheer curtain on the window.
A spot in the direct airflow from an AC ventMove the palm to a spot where you cannot feel the cold draught.
Cutting off yellow frondsLeave fronds until they are completely brown. The palm takes nutrients back from old fronds.
Feeding often or at full strengthA slow-release palm fertiliser two to three times a year in spring and summer (Clemson).

Areca Palm myths and facts

MythFact
An areca palm cleans the air in your home.A potted plant does not noticeably clean the air in a normal room. A 2019 review found that home and office ventilation removes pollutants far faster than plants do.
Cutting off yellow fronds helps an areca palm recover.It does the opposite. UF/IFAS found that regular removal of discoloured, potassium-deficient leaves speeds up the decline.
You can cut a tall areca palm back to make it bushier.Palms grow from a high central growing point, so they cannot be pruned back to reduce their height (Clemson).
Areca palms are toxic to cats and dogs.The ASPCA lists the areca palm as non-toxic to cats, dogs and horses.

Is an areca palm safe for cats and dogs?

Yes. The ASPCA lists the areca palm (Dypsis lutescens) as non-toxic to cats, dogs and horses. NC State Extension adds that the heart-of-palm (the growing point and young leaf buds) is cyanogenic and should not be eaten by people. Even a non-toxic plant can upset a pet's stomach if a lot is chewed.

If your pet chewed it: If your pet eats a lot of the plant and vomits or seems unwell, call your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic and tell them the plant name. If a child eats part of the plant, call your doctor or a poison centre.

Areca Palm FAQs

Can an areca palm live outside in the UAE?

Yes, an areca palm can live outside in the UAE in shade or partial shade. From May to September protect it from the midday and afternoon sun, because summer nights stay hot and pots dry out very fast. Move it outside gradually, not straight from an AC room. On the coast winter is mild, but inland and in colder GCC cities protect it on nights below 7 °C.

Does an areca palm clean the air?

An areca palm does not noticeably clean the air in a normal room. Chamber studies found that plants remove some chemicals, but a 2019 review (Cummings and Waring) showed that a home would need far more plants than anyone keeps to match normal ventilation. Choose an areca palm for its looks and because it is safe for pets.

How fast does an areca palm grow indoors?

Clemson Extension says areca palms grow about 15–25 cm (6–10 inches) a year and reach about 1.8–2.1 m (6–7 feet) indoors, so they often outgrow their space. In their native habitat in Madagascar they can reach about 9 m (30 feet).

Is an areca palm the same as a bamboo palm?

No, but the names overlap. NC State Extension and UF/IFAS list "bamboo palm" as a common name for the areca palm, because its clustered stems have rings like bamboo. The name is also used for two Chamaedorea palms, Chamaedorea seifrizii and the parlour palm (Chamaedorea elegans), which NC State notes are often confused with the areca palm. Both Chamaedorea palms tolerate lower light than an areca palm.

Can I cut back an areca palm that is too tall?

No. New growth comes from a high central growing point, so palms cannot be pruned back to reduce their height (Clemson Extension). Remove only completely dead fronds, give the palm more room, or divide a crowded clump.

Does an areca palm flower indoors?

Rarely. NC State Extension says areca palms will rarely bloom or produce fruit as a houseplant. Outdoors, mature palms produce hanging sprays of small flowers, followed by small egg-shaped fruits (NC State Extension, UF/IFAS).

Is an areca palm safe around young children?

NC State Extension rates the areca palm as a low-severity poison for people: the heart-of-palm is cyanogenic and can cause nausea and vomiting if eaten. Do not let young children chew the plant, and call your doctor or a poison centre if a child eats part of it.

Where does the areca palm come from?

The areca palm is native to eastern Madagascar, where UF/IFAS says it is endangered in the wild because its habitat is being lost. NC State Extension calls it one of the most popular indoor palms.

Ordering from PlantsWorld

How is plant size measured?

Size is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the top tip of the highest leaf. A plant listed as 50-60 CM stands in that range measured this way.

Which pot option should I choose, nursery or decorative?

Choose the nursery pot for the lowest price or if you already have a planter. Choose a decorative pot for a ready-to-display plant that arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer. The plant itself is the same.

Do the decorative pots have drainage holes?

Decorative pot orders include a drainage layer at the base, with premium soil mix and perlite. For specific details on a particular pot model, send us the product link and our team will confirm.

Is the plant healthy on arrival? Can I check first?

Plants are guaranteed to arrive healthy. Check your plant with the delivery agent: if it's damaged or not what you ordered, you can refuse it on the spot. If you find damage after unpacking, send photos and your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email sales@plantsworld.ae within 24 hours and we'll replace it free. You can also ask for a pre-dispatch photo.

My plant arrived with a few drooping or yellow leaves. Is that normal?

Yes, that's normal. A few drooping, bent or yellow leaves are a common reaction to the journey and a new spot, and plants usually recover within a few days. Keep it in bright indirect light and check the soil before watering. If the plant or pot is actually damaged, send photos within 24 hours.

Will my plant be safe in the UAE heat during delivery?

Yes. Our own delivery team brings your order, not a third-party courier. In extreme summer heat (June to September) we may move deliveries to farther emirates to a cooler day and agree the new day with you. If anything arrives damaged, we replace it free.

Will my plant look exactly like the website photo?

You'll receive the variety and size you ordered, but every plant grows individually, so leaf count, shape and shade can differ from the photo, which is representative. For peace of mind, ask for a pre-dispatch photo at checkout or on WhatsApp.

Something looks wrong with your plant?

Send us photos on WhatsApp and our team will tell you what is happening and what to do. These five photos help us answer fast:

  1. The whole plant, from a step back
  2. A close-up of the problem leaf, front and back
  3. The soil surface and the pot, with the drainage hole if there is one
  4. Where the plant stands: the window, the AC vent and the light
  5. When you last watered, and how much
